question: Should Telegram expose standalone pin/unpin message-tool actions, and what gate, default posture, and explicit-target semantics should protect them?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the feature expands agent authority over persistent Telegram chat state through bot credentials, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Approve gated explicit actions
options.body: Add Telegram-plugin-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind a pin-specific action gate, require explicit message ids unless separately approved, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Keep delivery pin only
options.body: Do not expose standalone pin/unpin actions yet; keep the current delivery-pin behavior for messages OpenClaw just sent.

options.title: Request design first
options.body: Ask for a short design covering admin-right expectations, per-account gating, forum-topic behavior, and implicit unpin semantics before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve gated explicit actions
recommendation.body: Add Telegram-plugin-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind a pin-specific action gate, require explicit message ids unless separately approved, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available owner for the product/security choice because recent Telegram action validation and this issue's review timeline point to that decision surface.
